caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2178 of 2009
lawyer:
Garib-E-Newaz, Advocate instructed by A.K.M. Shahidul Huq Advocate on Record ----- For the Petitioners 
Respondents ----- Not represented
parties:
Kadbanu Bibi and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Wazed Ali Sikder and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 25.05.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3610 of 1995)
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J.:- Instant application under Article 103 of the Constitution is directed against the judgment and order dated 25/05/2009 passed by the High Court Division discharging the rule issued in Civil Revision No. 3610 of 1995 thereby affirmed the judgment and decree dated 18/06/1995 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal, dismissing the Title Appeal No. 30 of 1992 affirming the judgment and decree dated 28/01/1992 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Mehendigonj, Barisal, decreeing the Title Suit No. 26 of 1990 declaring that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 76 of 1989 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Mehendigonj, Barisal, as illegal, collusive and void.

<u>2. The facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the instant petition are that the respondent No. 1 hereof as plaintiff filed the suit against the petitioner, as principal Defendant, and others contending, amongst others, that the schedule property in the suit belonged to petitioner No. 1 hereof, who entered into an agreement for sale of the same to the plaintiff-respondent hereof in 20.03.1989 on receipt of Tk. 1200/- as advance out of the consideration money and the possession was also delivered and thereafter on receipt of the balance of the consideration amount on 14.04.1985 required sale deed was duly executed and registered and accordingly the plaintiff got his name mutated in the records of right and have been paying the land revenue to the Government and that on or about 08.04.1990 the plaintiff came to know that the defendant-petitioner No. 1 hereof filed Title Suit No. 76 of 1989 without adding the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 hereof as a party in the suit and accordingly the plaintiff filed an application for adding him as a defendant in the suit, which was rejected on 09.04.1990 upon hearing the parties, and that on the same day a sole decree was passed in Title Suit No. 76 of 1989 on the basis of a compromise petition. The defendant No. 1-petitioner hereof claimed that he got the suit land by way of gift vide a registered heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 10.12.1981 from his minor son but the said minor son transferred the suit property along with other properties to the plaintiff prior to execution of the said heba deed and thus the heba deed was fraudulent, collusive and void document also being made without consideration and therefore the said son could not subsequently inherit the suit property from his mother the defendant No. 1, after her death, and that the decree in Title Suit No. 76 of 1989 was obtained on the basis of a solenama and that too by practicing fraud upon the Court and therefore the impugned decree is void, illegal, without jurisdiction and liable to be cancelled.</u>

3. The defendant No.1 petitioner hereof contested the suit by filling written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit property belonged to Azid Ali Bepari and that the defendant No. 1 was the wife of Azid Ali Bepari and that the said Azid Ali Bepari gifted the suit land in favour of the defendant No. 2, son of defendant No. 1 on 10.12.1981, who at the relevant time was a minor and delivery of possession was received by the defendant No. 1 on behalf of her minor son, the defendant No. 2, and accordingly they were enjoying usufructs from the suit land on payment land revenue and that the gift was genuine and that there was no act of fraud in the transfer through the heba deed and that the defendant No. 2 filed Title Suit No. 547 of 1983 for setting aside the heba deed and that by suppressing the service of summons of the case and playing fraud upon the Court obtained an exparte decree against the defendant No. 1 on 09.06.1986 and that thereafter for setting aside the said exparte decree the defendant No. 1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 76 of 1989 and that the defendant No. 1 though entered into a 2nd marriage yet used to visit her first husband's house regularly and she possessed the suit property along with other properties through her brothers. Azid Ali Bepari being defendant No. 1 in the said suit (Title Suit No. 76 of 1989) filed a solenama and accordingly the Title Suit No. 76 of 1989 was decreed on the basis of said solenama setting aside the decree passed in Title Suit No. 547 of 1983 and that the plaintiff was not made a party in said Title Suit No. 76 of 1989 and that the defendant No. 2 denied to have entered into any agreement with the plaintiff or executed any baina patra in respect of the said property and that the possession of suit property was never handed over to the plaintiff and that the sale deed dated 14.04.1985 is a collusive, void, antedated and illegal one and that the baina patra dated 20.03.1980 was a created document to undo the heba deed dated 10.12.1981.

4. On consideration of the materials and evidence on record and the submissions of the learned Advocate appearing for the respective parties, the learned Assistant Judge, decreed the suit on contest against the defendant-petitioner No. 1 hereof and exparte against the rest setting aside the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 76 of 1989 declaring the same to be void, illegal, collusive, without jurisdiction and nullity.

5. Being aggrieved, the defendant-petitioner No. 1 hereof filed Title Appeal No. 30 of 1992 before the learned District Judge, Barisal, and the said appeal, on transfer, was heard and dismissed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal, and that in the appeal the petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 were added as appellant Nos. 2 and 3 claiming to have become owners in some part of the suit property by purchase from the defendant-petitioner No. 1 hereof and that being aggrieved by such dismissal the defendant-appellant-petitioners hereof moved the High Court Division in civil Revision No. 3610 of 1995 and upon hearing, the Rule, issued therein, has been discharged by the High Court Division by the judgment and order impugned in the instant civil petition.

6. We have perused the leave petition and the judgments of the Courts below as annexed to the petition as well as the provisions of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and considered the submissions of the learned Advocate.

7. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that the suit being a suit for declaration simplicitor is not maintainable as per provisions of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act inasmuch as in the prayer portion of the plaintiff in the suit land and that the Appellate Division in several cases has held that a suit in which title of the plaintiff has been disputed by the defendant, a declaration of title and possession is necessary and in the absence of a prayer for such declaration such suit is not maintainable in view of the provision to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and hence the decree as passed is illegal and not maintainable.

8. It appears from the judgment of the trial Court that specific issue was framed being issue No. 4. “বাদীর নালিশী জমিতে স্বত্ত্ব দখল আছে কি? and that the contesting parties in the suit have contested the said issue with evidence and that the trial Court on consideration of the materials and evidence on record as well as the submissions made by the learned Advocates of the contesting parties found the title and possession of the plaintiff on the suit land and further it appears that though in the prayer portion such specific prayer for declaration title and possession was not made but in the body of the plaint the title and possession of the plaintiff was claimed and that since the question of title and possession was made an issue in deciding that suit and contesting the parties without raising any objection contested the same being issue No. 4 quoted above and the trial Court on consideration of the materials and evidence on record found the title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit, the defect as alleged was cured, more so when no objection was raised against such defect in the suit and when no objection was raised against the framing of said issue No. 4. It seems that the trial Court on its wisdom to adjudicate the case property, on consideration of the pleadings of the parties, framed the said issue No. 4 in accordance with law.

<u>9. We are of the view that the decisions of the Appellate Division on the point of maintainability referring to Section-42 of the Specific Relief Act, as submitted by the learned Advocate, are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case and that in fact the contesting parties were given due opportunity to contest the issue framed to decide the title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. It further appears that the appellate Court below also considered the issue of title and possession of the plaintiff respondent No. 1 hereof on the suit land and found that the impugned gift deed to be a void document since the recipient was minor at the relevant time and had no occasion to purchase any 'jainamaz' and deliver the same as consideration for the gift, as alleged, and that the Appellate Court below in detail discussed the case as well as the evidence available on record and dismissed the appeal with cost affirming the judgment of the trial Court. It also appears that the High Court Division has considered all aspects of the cases, including the issue No. 4 framed and decided by the trial Court, in the following manner:</u>

<u>"On appeal, it appears, the learned Appellate Court also considering the evidence and materials on record came to the finding that the plaintiff acquired title in the suit land by registered kabala dated 24.04.1985 executed and registered by Aid Ali and that the plaintiff has been in possession of the suit land since then and that Kadbanu or Kadam Ali did not acquire any title in the suit land by heba-bil-ewaj dated 10.12.1981 and that Kadam Ali being minor at the relevant time had no capacity to give Jainamaj and Tasbih' in exchange of the gift and that no possession was handed over to Kadbanu Bibi or Kadam Ali and that the defendant did not produce the original heba-bil-ewaj deed in the Court, but produced the certified copy of the same and that Azid Ali knew to give his signature but he has executed the heba-bil-ewaj deed by putting thump impression and that the heba-bil-ewaj deed was not acted upon. On these findings the learned appellate Court dismissed the appeal. It appears, the present suit is a suit for declaration that the decree dated 09.04.1990 passed in Title Suit No. 76 of 1989 is void, fraudulent and not binding on the plaintiff as he was not made party in the said suit though he claims to be the owner of the suit land by registered deed dated 14.04.1985. Both the Courts found that the present plaintiff was a necessary party in the said suit, but he was not made party and that his application for addition of party was rejected by the trial Court. The case of the defendant is that the suit as framed is not maintainable. According to the learned Advocate for the petitioner the defendants having challenged the right, title and possession of the plaintiff in the present suit, the plaintiff ought to have prayed for declaration of his title in the suit land along with the prayer for declaration that the decree dated 09.04.1990 is void. According to the learned Advocate in the present suit no prayer for declaration of title having been made, the present suit for declaration that the decree dated 09.04.1990 is void is not maintainable. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred to the decision of Ratan Chandra Dey and others Vs. Jinnator Nahar and others reported in 13 MLR (AD) 168 and the decision of Md. Jashimuddin (Kanchan) Vs. Md. Ali Ashraf reported in 11 BLD (AD) 101 wherein there lordships of the Appellate Division held that when the defendant in his written statement claim title and possession in the suit land, a simple suit for declaration that a decree or a deed is void is not maintainable, without first establishing his title to the suit land. The proposition of law as has been decided in the said 2 decisions are not disputed, but in the present case both the Courts correctly found that the plaintiff was able to prove his title and possession in the suit land. It may be noted that the trial Court framed issue No. 4 to the effect that whether the plaintiff has got right, title and possession in the suit land and the trial Court on consideration of the evidence and materials on record specifically found that the plaintiff has got title and possession in the suit land. Since in the present suit an issue has been framed as to the title and possession of the plaintiff and both the Courts found that he got right, title and possession in the suit land, in my opinion, further declaration regarding title of the plaintiff is not essential in the present suit land as such in the absence of such prayer for declaration of title, the present suit as framed in also maintainable. Thus it shows that the facts of the present case is distinguishable from the facts of the above reported eases and as such, in my opinion those decisions are not applicable in the present case."</u>

<u>10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and as the contesting parties contested the issue No. 4 as to the title and possession on the suit land, having had all opportunities, we do agree with the findings and decision of the High Court Division and further we are of the view that the objection as raised by the learned Advocate referring to Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act at this stage do not merit any consideration in the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed hereinabove.</u>

11. Accordingly no interference with the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is called for.

12. Accordingly, the leave petition is dismissed.

End.
